rows: Morgan Stanley Global Consumer & Retail Conference
South Florida Market Share (#2, passed Monster)
Handful of markets in 2024; sizable rollout over 3-5 yrs
First full year inside the PepsiCo system - became the #3 energy player, reaching ~9%-9.5% Nielsen tracked share (higher in Circana) from ~3.5%.
Revenue on track to more than double in 2023.

Tracked-channel share flattened sequentially at 9%-9.5% since early August - management attributes it to Q4 seasonality, holiday-floor compression, and competitive 'noise' (Red Bull and Alani Nu seasonal launches), not a structural slowdown.
Management urged investors to view historical Q4s as a guide and expects Q1 and Q2 2024 to 'shape up.'
2024 spring resets (Jan-May) are the first fully integrated Pepsi planning cycle - expected to deliver more and better space, more SKUs and slots; management declined to quantify.
Foodservice grew from 'next to nothing' to ~10% of Pepsi's delivered revenue - outpacing what Bang ever achieved at Rockstar; QSR runway (Taco Bell, Pizza Hut).
Demographic much broader than the energy category - 'a full beverage play,' aging down (18-24 entering) and up; 75-80% of growth incremental, 50/50 male/female.
GLP-1 drugs viewed as an opportunity - fatigued patients consuming fewer calories should benefit the energy category; Celsius's fitness 'healthy halo' positions it as a likely top beneficiary.

Bang's potential revival: Celsius was the biggest beneficiary of Bang's shelf space (not consumers) and will not cede it back; Bang's resurgence a bigger risk to Monster's own portfolio (and C4/Ghost).
Pricing seen as a 2024 opportunity following Red Bull's price move ('five weeks in,' need a couple months to see if it sticks); a second consecutive year of category pricing could establish a trend.

Velocity accelerated even as distribution expanded massively - credited to wiring into the Pepsi system without disruption, best-in-class merchandising, and influencer/digital-heavy marketing plus MLS and F1/Ferrari partnerships.
South Florida playbook (24% share, passed Monster) being replicated across 30 drill-deep markets; the brand 'travels' (strong share even in non-drill-deep Buffalo).
Management declines to commit to a quantified 2024 margin path - 'in growth mode,' 'not ready to draw a line in the sand'; prioritizes share gains over margin expansion.
Margin levers cited: orbit freight model, normalized raw materials, flushing costly international cans, co-packer relationships, procurement/manufacturing scale, promo-calendar efficiency.
Celsius is roughly at Monster's total-company gross margin on a freight-adjusted basis but well below Monster's high-60s US margins; closing the gap will take time as growth moderates.
Club and Amazon use a different (full-pallet, no white-glove) model with cost savings partly shared back - net gross margin profile consistent channel to channel.
#1 on Amazon in energy (ahead of Red Bull, passed Monster in Q3); a top-selling beverage at Costco overall; 'middle innings' at Sam's Club.
Clean-energy competitors (Ghost, Alani, C4) are solid brands with narrower demographics; Celsius's fitness authenticity drives a better-for-you spillover and incremental category growth.
Energy is gaining shelf space at the expense of CSDs, dairy, teas, and coffee; failed small brands create space opportunities for Celsius.
2024 innovation: line bifurcation (core vs Vibe), ESSENTIALS 16oz nationwide rollout, SKUs coming off 7-Eleven/Circle K exclusivity, two Vibe SKUs, variety packs.
Primary focus remains growing the core portfolio - 'we feel like this is a unicorn' and 'don't feel like a 10 share is nearly good enough.'
Frame the growth opportunities ahead - distribution breadth, depth, velocity, non-tracked channels, international - and what is most important to the long-term profile as Celsius scales.

Opportunity exists across all areas. ACV is in a strong place; 2024 resets run Jan-May, offering more/better space, SKUs and slots. Foodservice grew from next to nothing to ~10% of Pepsi's delivered revenue with QSR runway. Non-tracked C&G can reach a couple hundred thousand Pepsi locations. Drill-deep expands from 6 (2020) to 18 (2022) to 30 (2024). International is 'a couple of years away' but has runway.
Why tracked-channel share has been range-bound at 9%-9.5% since early August and when it would move higher.

Attributed the plateau to 'a lot of noise in the category' and Q4 seasonality, which affects Celsius more than peers because its sales team drives large display drops competing with holiday floor merchandising. Cited Red Bull's seasonal SKU and Alani Nu's two launches (a seasonal and the Kim Kardashian 'Kimade' SKU). Urged investors to view historical Q4s as a guide; expects Q1 and Q2 to 'shape up.'
In the first fully integrated Pepsi planning cycle, an early read on the percentage of accounts resetting space for spring and how much incremental space Celsius is getting.

Declined specifics ('we don't really give guidance') but said management is 'pleased' and expects more/better space across all channels, with earlier planogram access and better placement. Visible innovation: ESSENTIALS 16oz line (four SKUs, adding a fifth) nationwide in January, SKUs coming off 7-Eleven/Circle K exclusivity, two Vibe SKUs (noncarbonated and core), and variety packs.
How to size the opportunity in non-tracked Pepsi channels (colleges, hospitals, hotels) and the initial consumer pull at foodservice wins like Jersey Mike's and Dunkin'.

Foodservice was 'really nonexistent' before the Pepsi deal and is hard to size, but reaching 10% of Pepsi's revenue contribution is significant and outpaced what Bang ever achieved at Rockstar. Celsius is in 2,000-plus Jersey Mike's locations with encouraging early data - a potential QSR proof of concept (Taco Bell, Pizza Hut). Entered Dunkin' nationally with one SKU.
A snapshot of Celsius's demographic profile vs traditional energy, how it is changing as the brand scales from 3% to 9-10% share, and the long-term growth implications.

Celsius's demographic is much broader than the energy category - essentially a full beverage play, aging down (18-24 entering) and up, with 75-80% of growth incremental to the brand and a 50/50 male/female split. Targeting is community-based via the 30-market drill-deep strategy and partnerships (MLS, F1).
How Celsius is thinking about the GLP-1 (Ozempic/Wegovy) opportunity, given energy-drink consumption could rise among fatigued patients.

Celsius will not revert to its calorie-burning positioning but agreed GLP-1 is an opportunity - patients consuming fewer calories produce less energy, so the category should benefit, and Celsius's fitness-rooted 'healthy halo' positions it as a likely top beneficiary.
The risk to Celsius's growth if Monster successfully revitalizes the Bang brand, given Celsius disproportionately benefited from Bang's decline.

Celsius was the biggest beneficiary of Bang's shelf space (not its consumers) as the #3 player and 'next man up,' and will not cede that space back. Bang's resurgence is more a risk to Monster's own portfolio (and to C4 and Ghost) than to Celsius.
Midterm international market-share targets, what level of share makes a market worthwhile, and the expected incremental investment.

Monster derives ~35-37% of revenue internationally and took time to ramp; today's digital/social tools allow faster brand-awareness building. Celsius will be methodical, working with Pepsi's multi-country partners to build playbooks - a handful of markets in 2024, faster rollout in 2025-2026. Investments will be 'modest' and not materially impactful over the next couple of years; a sizable rollout expected across roughly six core partners over three to five years.
How Celsius is thinking about pricing opportunities, given it was restrained on pricing in 2023 and Red Bull recently moved on price.

It is 'five weeks in' on Red Bull's move and needs a couple of months to see if it sticks. Pricing is an opportunity; the CPG market typically has annual price increases while energy has differed. Two consecutive years of category pricing could establish a trend, and as the super-premium brand, Celsius's elasticity will be interesting to test - a 2024 opportunity.
What drove the unusual acceleration in velocity even as distribution expanded massively, and the view on velocity growth in 2024 and beyond.

Credited the marketing/sales organizations for wiring into the Pepsi system without disruption, Pepsi's best-in-class merchandising, and influencer-heavy, digital-heavy marketing plus MLS and F1/Ferrari partnerships. Celsius replicates its proven core-market playbook (24% share in South Florida, passed Monster) across 30 drill-deep markets in 2024; strong share even in non-drill-deep markets like Buffalo shows the brand 'travels.'
Given the CFO's Q3 caution against expecting more incremental margin improvement, the broader puts and takes for 2024 gross margin.

Management does not want to set expectations that get investors 'over their skis' and will not decide based on consensus. There is opportunity to 'slowly turn the screws,' but Celsius is in growth mode prioritizing share gains. Levers: orbit freight model, normalized raw materials, flushing costly international cans, co-packer relationships, procurement/manufacturing scale, promo-calendar efficiency - but 'not ready to draw a line in the sand.'
Given Celsius is roughly at Monster's total-company gross margin on a freight-adjusted basis but well below Monster's high-60s US margins, how much of that gap it could close.

Monster sets the standard and is used as a goal; Celsius believes it can get there over time. Opportunities exist across procurement, manufacturing-partner capacity utilization (longer runs), and promos as Celsius scales; as growth moderates, management will fine-tune to capture leverage.
The growth potential in Club and e-commerce channels and how grocery and C-stores compare on profitability.

Club and Amazon use a different model - full-pallet, no white-glove service - so there are cost savings partly shared back to the retailer; net gross margin profile is consistent channel to channel. Celsius is #1 on Amazon in energy (ahead of Red Bull, passed Monster in Q3), a top-selling beverage at Costco overall, and in 'middle innings' at Sam's Club. C-store trial drives subsequent bulk-pack purchases at Amazon/Costco/Sam's.
What differentiates Celsius from clean/performance-energy competitors (Ghost, Alani, C4) and whether they are share competition or category-growth contributors.

Those are solid brands but each has a narrower demographic than Celsius; Alani doesn't play well in fitness, while Ghost and C4 are fitness-channel players. Celsius's authenticity is rooted in fitness, creating a better-for-you spillover. Celsius aims to take share from everybody and is incremental, bringing in new consumers at a higher rate than any other brand. Energy is gaining shelf space at the expense of CSDs, dairy, teas, and coffee.
The innovation strategy and pipeline for 2024 and the medium term, and where Celsius sits between Red Bull's and Monster's portfolio strategies.

2024 has substantial innovation. In 2023 Celsius bifurcated its lines - separating core SKUs (fruit on package) from Vibe lines (same formula, different flavor/marketing) - to win additional shelf space per line. The ESSENTIALS 16oz line launched at 7-Eleven and rolls out nationwide. Innovation is evaluated for energy-category levers and large-TAM adjacencies, but the primary focus remains growing the core portfolio ('this is a unicorn'; a 10 share is not the ceiling).
